description: Patch releases of YOURLS are automerged once CI is green by extending the shared `patch-automerge` preset. Minor and major releases still require manual review.

YOURLS has carried schema migrations in patch releases and cannot apply them unattended. Its `YOURLS_DB_VERSION` moved 506 -> 507 between 1.10.2 and 1.10.3, and a fresh-install Molecule run cannot exercise that upgrade path. Enabling patch automerge accepts that an existing installation may need a manual visit to `/admin/upgrade.php` after deployment.

The Molecule suite installs YOURLS, asserts the admin area is past the installer rather than 307-redirecting to it, verifies that the application-reported version belongs to the pinned release while allowing only a terminal `-dev` suffix, creates a short URL over the API with the credentials the role wrote into `env`, follows the short URL to its target without following redirects, and reads the URL and exact application-reported version back out of MariaDB under a non-default database name and table prefix.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the Docker Hub noise out. `yourls` publishes 84 tags, of which strict semver leaves only the real x.y.z releases: the `-apache`, `-fpm` and `-fpm-alpine` flavours parse as prereleases and are skipped, while `latest`, `apache`, `fpm`, `1` and `1.10` are not versions at all. The bare, unsuffixed tag this role uses does exist for every release, so nothing real is filtered out.

customManagers.description: Upstream's container build recipe lives on the untagged `dist` branch of YOURLS/containers, so `yourls_container_image_self_build_repo_version` is a commit SHA rather than a version and the shared annotation-driven manager cannot track it. Pinned by hand until now, it silently stayed on 1.10.3's recipe while yourls_version had already moved to 1.10.4, so self-building operators quietly got the older YOURLS.

packageRules.description: A YOURLS release and upstream's build recipe for it are published by the same automation minutes apart, so their updates travel in one branch instead of racing each other into separate ones.

The self-build recipe revision is grouped with the corresponding YOURLS release. Allowing this digest update to automerge prevents it from vetoing patch automerge for the group; a grouped minor or major release remains manual because its YOURLS update is not automerge-enabled.
